formats.key: Permit(address owner,address spender,uint256 value,uint256 nonce,uint256 deadline)
effects: Once the spender submits it, the signature sets the owner's Linea bridged DAI allowance for `spender` to exactly `value`. It replaces the old allowance; it does not add to it (ERC20Upgradeable._approve via ERC20PermitUpgradeable.permit).
If `value` is type(uint256).max, the allowance never goes down when spent; any smaller value goes down as the spender uses it (_spendAllowance).
The signature only works until `deadline` (require(block.timestamp <= deadline)).
Using the signature spends the owner's current nonce, so the owner's other unused permit signatures with that nonce stop working (_useNonce).
No tokens move when the permit is used. The spender can later pull up to `value` DAI from the owner with transferFrom.
formats.shown: The screen says 'Authorize spending of tokens' and shows the spender address, the maximum amount in DAI (or 'Unlimited' at or above 2^255), the expiry date and the owner.

findings.title: Permit has no interpolatedIntent, so the intent line names neither the token amount nor the spender.
findings.evidence: descriptor.json: "intent": "Authorize spending of tokens" and no interpolatedIntent. Case 0 screen intent is 'Authorize spending of tokens'; the amount '250 DAI' and spender 0x1111…0582 appear only in the fields.
